title: The word didn't exist yet.
description:
The word didn't exist yet. 'Spam' wasn't coined for unwanted online messages until April 1993, on Usenet, fifteen years after this email was sent.

A marketing manager at Digital Equipment Corporation. On 3 May, he pitched a new DEC computer to roughly 400 people over ARPANET, the internet's forerunner.

Thuerk himself recalled, decades later. A few days after, an ARPANET representative phoned him directly. 'He made me promise never to do it again,' Thuerk said.

US dollars in sales DEC reportedly made off that single unsolicited pitch.

The complaint that got him in trouble is also why he's remembered today as spam's accidental inventor.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_email_spam: confirms the 3 May 1978 DEC advertisement for its DECSYSTEM-20 products, sent by Gary Thuerk with colleague Carl Gartley sending it from Thuerk's own account, to roughly 400 ARPANET users, the reported $13 million in resulting sales, and that the term 'spam' itself was not coined for this kind of message until April 1993 on Usenet, fifteen years later.
- https://www.weforum.org/stories/industries-in-depth/its-40-years-since-the-first-spam-email-was-sent-here-are-6-things-you-didnt: independently corroborates the 1978 date, the roughly 400 recipients and the $13 million sales figure, and carries Thuerk's own quotes, 'complaints started coming in almost immediately' and his account of an ARPANET representative phoning him: 'He made me promise never to do it again.'
